module_title: The Supremes: First, Largest, and Most Famous
introduction: India possesses a massive network of Protected Areas. At this level, we focus on the absolute basics: the national parks that hold a 'superlative' title (first, largest, smallest) and those uniquely famous worldwide.

core_concepts.title: The First and The Oldest
core_concepts.description: **Jim Corbett National Park** (Uttarakhand): Established in 1936, it is India's first National Park. Its original name was 'Hailey National Park'. The Ramganga river flows through it.

core_concepts.title: Largest and Smallest
core_concepts.description:
1. **Largest:** **Hemis National Park** (Ladakh). It is the largest national park in India and is globally famous for its Snow Leopard population. 
2. **Smallest:** **South Button Island National Park** (Andaman and Nicobar Islands).

core_concepts.title: The World's Only Floating Park
core_concepts.description: **Keibul Lamjao National Park** (Manipur). It is located on the Loktak Lake. It is the only floating national park in the world and the last natural habitat of the endangered 'Sangai' (Dancing Deer).

core_concepts.title: Single-Species Havens
core_concepts.description:
1. **Kaziranga National Park** (Assam): Famous for the Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceros. 
2. **Gir National Park** (Gujarat): The *only* natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in the world.

important_entities.name: Project Tiger
important_entities.significance: A major exam favorite. The Government of India launched Project Tiger in 1973 (from Jim Corbett National Park) to promote conservation of the Bengal Tiger.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Students often guess large states like Rajasthan or Maharashtra. The state with the highest number of National Parks (and maximum forest cover) is **Madhya Pradesh**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Hemis is in Ladakh (High altitude), and it has the 'Highest' area (Largest National Park).

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed SSC and Railway question: 'Which is the only floating national park in the world?' Answer: Keibul Lamjao (Manipur).
